feature: SMARCB1 G344Afs*13 (plasma ctDNA, pathogenic) - hypothesised SMARCB1/INI1 deficiency, UNCONFIRMED
test_name: INI1/SMARCB1 IHC (BAF47/SNF5 antibody, clone 25 or MRQ-27) on tumor tissue, scored against the internal positive control
tissue_type: archival FFPE; 2026 pulmonary core and 2024 uterine block
rationale: Complete loss of nuclear INI1 in tumor cells, with staining retained in the lymphocytes, endothelium and stroma that serve as the internal control, is what turns the plasma SMARCB1 frameshift into a target; the tazemetostat basket study required loss by IHC, or biallelic molecular loss where IHC was equivocal (NCT02601950). Retained nuclear INI1 closes the EZH2 branch outright. Set expectations either way: in that study's INI1-negative cohort outside epithelioid sarcoma the response rate was 9 percent (PMID 41882006), and 170 uterine smooth-muscle tumors in a consecutive series all retained SMARCB1 (PMID 34271067).
turnaround_estimate: 3-5 days once the block is in hand; request block release first, which is usually the slow step
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 2 unstained slides, ordered on both the 2026 pulmonary core and the 2024 uterine block
decision_gated: Tazemetostat (off-label or via an INI1-negative cohort of the type used in NCT02601950); a retained stain closes the branch.

notes: Read the four possible outcomes before ordering. Loss with a clean internal control means SMARCB1/INI1 deficiency and the branch opens. Retained staining has three readings that are not interchangeable: a subclonal SMARCB1 event present in a metastasis not represented by the stained block, a monoallelic frameshift on a background of retained protein (a truncating call at one allele does not require protein loss), or a plasma variant that never came from this tumor at all, which is the same failure mode the TP53 call carries. Equivocal or weak staining is not a negative and is exactly the situation the trial language routes to molecular confirmation. Tissue order B, the one IHC block cut: INI1/SMARCB1, MMR (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6), p53, Rb, ATRX, PD-L1 and B7-H3.

Ordering the stain first and the panel only if it is positive costs two to three weeks and can strand the case in an equivocal stain with no molecular backup, which is the specific delay this patient cannot absorb with induction pending.

feature: Remaining unmeasured molecular landscape (the gap has narrowed, not closed)
test_name: RNA-based fusion NGS panel covering NTRK1, NTRK2 and NTRK3 (with RET, ALK and ROS1 in the same run) on archival tissue
rationale: What is on file is non-detection on a plasma DNA assay at unstated tumor fraction, which is not a negative: plasma fusion calling is insensitive when shedding is low, and DNA capture misses breakpoints in the large NTRK introns. RNA sequencing reads the transcript and so is agnostic to where in the intron the break sits, which is what allows a negative to be read as a negative. Prevalence in uterine leiomyosarcoma is very low, but a spindle-cell tumor once signed out as benign is precisely the setting in which an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal neoplasm hides, and a positive converts a chemotherapy-only landscape into an oral TRK inhibitor.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; shares the specimen with tissue order A. RNA quality degrades in blocks older than about 5 years, so the 2026 lung core is the safer input
decision_gated: Larotrectinib, entrectinib or repotrectinib under the tumor-agnostic NTRK fusion indications.

Skipping it leaves the one non-cytotoxic branch in this case unopened at the point where LMS-04 fails.

feature: High-grade uterine leiomyosarcoma histology
test_name: Baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with LVEF and global longitudinal strain
rationale: A documented pre-treatment LVEF is the precondition for giving doxorubicin, and the LMS-04 schedule carries the anthracycline to a cumulative dose in the cardiotoxicity surveillance band (PMID 35835135). ASCO and the 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guideline both call for baseline ventricular imaging, with strain where available, before anthracycline exposure (PMID 27918725; PMID 36017568). Nothing cardiac is on file, so cycle 1 would be given with no reference value against which a later fall in function could be read.
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; transthoracic echocardiogram (5-10 mL blood only if natriuretic peptides are added)
decision_gated: Fitness for doxorubicin in the planned LMS-04 induction, and the reference LVEF for on-treatment monitoring.
notes: Done at the treating institution rather than a send-out laboratory, hence no provider list. Add natriuretic peptide and troponin at the same visit if a cardio-oncology service wants a biochemical baseline. Time-critical: induction is planned and not started.

feature: High-grade uterine leiomyosarcoma histology
test_name: Baseline comprehensive metabolic panel with bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, transaminases, creatine kinase and calculated creatinine clearance, plus a CBC with differential read against an altitude-adjusted haemoglobin reference
rationale: Trabectedin carries dose-limiting hepatotoxicity and rhabdomyolysis risk, so baseline transaminases, bilirubin and creatine kinase are what any on-treatment abnormality will be measured against; LMS-04 gave the combination first line and carried trabectedin into maintenance (PMID 35835135). No laboratory values were supplied at intake, so there is currently no baseline at all. Residence at roughly 8,500 feet raises expected haemoglobin, and reading her count against a sea-level reference will make real chemotherapy-induced anaemia look like a normal result.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood plus a serum tube at the pre-treatment visit
decision_gated: Fitness for trabectedin dosing and the reference values for on-treatment hepatic, renal and haematologic monitoring.
notes: Local phlebotomy, hence no provider list. Ask the reporting laboratory to flag the altitude of residence on the requisition, or record the expected shift in the chart, so the haemoglobin is not read flat against a sea-level interval.

feature: Remaining unmeasured molecular landscape (the gap has narrowed, not closed)
test_name: Paired peripheral-blood leukocyte sequencing (buffy-coat myeloid/CHIP panel covering TP53) plus tissue NGS interrogation of the TP53 Q52* position
tissue_type: whole blood (buffy coat) and archival FFPE
rationale: Two orthogonal routes settle this and either will do: the same TP53 Q52* found in tumor DNA makes it tumor-derived, while finding it in white-cell DNA makes it clonal haematopoiesis. That distinction is not academic at unstated tumor fraction; in matched cfDNA and white-blood-cell sequencing, 53.2 percent of cfDNA mutations in cancer patients had features of clonal haematopoiesis (PMID 31768066). Be honest about the payoff: a confirmed somatic TP53 in uterine leiomyosarcoma is expected and largely prognostic, so the value is in calibrating how much weight the rest of this plasma report, including the SMARCB1 call, can carry.

feature: HLA-A*02:01 confirmed present - opens the A*02:01-restricted TCR-T axis, one step behind antigen-expression testing
test_name: MAGE-A4 expression by IHC on tumor tissue, scored to the SPEARHEAD-1 screening threshold of at least 1+ staining in at least 10 percent of cells
rationale: The expensive half of the eligibility question is already answered, since allele-level typing confirms A*02:01, one of the four allele groups the approved MAGE-A4 product names (A*02:01P, A*02:02P, A*02:03P, A*02:06P). What remains is antigen expression, and the threshold is protocol-specified rather than a local judgement call: SPEARHEAD-1 required at least 1+ staining in at least 10 percent of cells by central IHC (NCT04044768), and the licensed indication requires expression by an FDA-approved or cleared companion diagnostic. A multi-subtype sarcoma IHC series found MAGE-A4 expressed in only a minority of smooth-muscle sarcomas (PMID 40152485), well short of the near-uniform positivity that defines the synovial sarcoma population these products were built around, so a negative here is a realistic and useful outcome that closes the branch.
turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks locally; central-laboratory screening runs on the sponsor's clock
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 3-5 unstained slides, shared with the PRAME and NY-ESO-1 stains on one block cut
decision_gated: MAGE-A4-directed TCR-T (uzatresgene autoleucel and successor solid-tumor programs); afamitresgene autoleucel itself is licensed for synovial sarcoma only.

feature: Bilateral pulmonary metastases with an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory radiologic pattern
test_name: Pre-treatment CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with measurable RECIST v1.1 target lesions, read against any imaging available from the September 2024 to July 2026 interval
rationale: Trial screening requires measurable disease by RECIST v1.1, and an infiltrative pulmonary pattern is exactly the morphology that can fail to yield measurable target lesions; better to discover that before a screening slot than during one. Reading the baseline against anything shot in the 2024 to 2026 interval also bounds the growth kinetics of disease that went untreated for roughly 23 months, which is the single best available estimate of tempo. Abdomen and pelvis matter here specifically because the 2024 hysterectomy may have disrupted the specimen.
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; cross-sectional imaging with contrast unless contraindicated
decision_gated: RECIST measurability for trial screening, response assessment during LMS-04, and the field of view for excluding peritoneal disease.
notes: Ask the radiologist to name and record target lesions explicitly rather than describing the burden qualitatively. If no lesion is measurable, that is a finding worth surfacing now, since it narrows the trial set independent of any biomarker.

feature: ~23-month interval between resection of the primary (September 2024, signed out benign) and correct diagnosis (July-August 2026)
test_name: Retrieval of the September 2024 operative report and gross pathology description: route of hysterectomy, whether power or manual morcellation was used, specimen integrity and margin status
tissue_type: no tissue; operative and gross pathology records
rationale: A 6.0 cm myometrial mass removed as a presumed benign fibroid in 2024 may have been morcellated, and morcellation of an unrecognised leiomyosarcoma disperses tumor through the peritoneum and has been associated with worse outcomes (PMID 28209496; PMID 26646120). The staging picture is currently pulmonary only; if the specimen was disrupted, peritoneal and pelvic disease has to be actively excluded rather than assumed absent. The answer sits in an operative note nobody has yet had reason to re-read.
tissue_required_estimate: no tissue; the operative note and gross description from the September 2024 hysterectomy
decision_gated: Whether peritoneal and pelvic disease must be actively excluded, and how the staging imaging field is drawn.
notes: Records retrieval, hence no provider list. Send one letter to the 2024 institution covering both the operative note and the release of the paraffin block, since the block is needed for tissue orders A and B anyway.

feature: SMARCB1 G344Afs*13 (plasma ctDNA, pathogenic) - hypothesised SMARCB1/INI1 deficiency, UNCONFIRMED
test_name: Germline SMARCB1 sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis on whole blood, reflexed if tumor INI1 is lost or biallelic SMARCB1 loss is confirmed
rationale: Germline SMARCB1 loss underlies rhabdoid tumor predisposition and schwannomatosis, and a uterine leiomyosarcoma arising in a schwannomatosis patient with a SMARCB1 alteration has been reported (PMID 26001331). A woman in her thirties with a confirmed tumor SMARCB1 event is exactly the presentation where somatic-only testing leaves both her own surveillance and her relatives' unanswered. Reflex this rather than ordering it up front: without tissue confirmation the pretest probability does not justify the counselling burden.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA, or saliva where a blood draw is inconvenient
decision_gated: Family screening and her own surveillance if tumor INI1 loss is confirmed; no therapeutic gate.

providers.name: Ambry Genetics
providers.notes: Carries SMARCB1 on both the expanded panel and as a single gene with deletion/duplication analysis, so the order can be scoped once the tissue result is known.

providers.name: Myriad Genetics
providers.address: 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: Deletion/duplication analysis matters here; whole-gene and multi-exon SMARCB1 deletions are a recognised germline mechanism and sequence-only testing would miss them. Pair the requisition with the HRR germline panel below so she gives blood once.

feature: Remaining unmeasured molecular landscape (the gap has narrowed, not closed)
test_name: Germline multigene hereditary cancer panel including BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2, RAD51C, RAD51D, ATM, TP53 and the Lynch genes
rationale: Somatic-only testing answers what the tumor carries and nothing about what she carries, which for a woman in her thirties leaves her own second-cancer risk and her relatives' screening open. A germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 finding would also strengthen the PARP-inhibitor case beyond what a somatic call alone supports (PMID 37467452). Run it on the same draw as any other blood work rather than as a reflex weeks later; the counselling and insurance steps are the slow part, not the assay.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood in EDTA, or saliva
decision_gated: Strength of the PARP-inhibitor case, plus cascade testing and her own surveillance.

providers.name: Myriad Genetics
providers.address: 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.notes: Broadest payer coverage of the group for a patient with no family history documented, which is the practical bottleneck here rather than assay quality.

notes: Include TP53 on the panel. Sarcoma in a woman under 40 is a Li-Fraumeni-pattern presentation, and a germline TP53 result would change her imaging surveillance and argue against radiotherapy where it is avoidable, which bears directly on the SBRT option the treating oncologist has kept open. Combine the requisition with germline SMARCB1 if the tissue result calls for it.

feature: HLA-A*02:01 confirmed present - opens the A*02:01-restricted TCR-T axis, one step behind antigen-expression testing
test_name: NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B) expression by IHC (clone E978) or RT-PCR, run on the same block as MAGE-A4 and PRAME
rationale: Her A*02:01 satisfies the restriction requirement for the NY-ESO-1 TCR-T program, which enrols A*02:01, A*02:05 or A*02:06 positive patients with central-laboratory-confirmed NY-ESO-1 expression (NCT03967223). Two things hold this below the other two antigens: NY-ESO-1 expression was low across all sarcoma subtypes in a recent multi-subtype IHC series (PMID 40152485), and that master protocol restricts enrolment to synovial sarcoma and myxoid/round cell liposarcoma, so even a positive stain points to a future solid-tumor cohort rather than an open door. It earns its place only because it adds one stain to a block already being cut.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; no additional specimen beyond the cancer/testis antigen block cut
decision_gated: NY-ESO-1-directed TCR-T (letetresgene autoleucel); trial-only, and currently histology-restricted away from leiomyosarcoma.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Same requisition as MAGE-A4 and PRAME; ordering the three separately is the mistake this row is trying to prevent.

feature: High-grade uterine leiomyosarcoma histology
test_name: Formal grading parameters from the reference pathology review: mitotic index per 10 high-power fields, coagulative tumor cell necrosis, nuclear atypia and FNCLCC grade, on both specimens
tissue_type: archival FFPE; existing slides, no new cut required
rationale: The diagnosis itself is settled: a reference laboratory confirmed uterine leiomyosarcoma on both the pulmonary biopsy and the re-reviewed uterine specimen in August 2026, so no second opinion is needed. What is not on file are the numbers behind the phrase high-grade, and trial screening asks for FNCLCC grade rather than a descriptor. Retrieving them is a request for a report, not a new assay, and it also documents whether the 2024 block was adequately sampled for a mass that went unrecognised at first pass.
turnaround_estimate: days; a report request rather than new testing
tissue_required_estimate: no new tissue; the existing reference-laboratory report and slides
decision_gated: Trial eligibility fields that ask for FNCLCC grade, and prognostic framing of the disease tempo.
notes: Ask the reference laboratory that signed the August 2026 review, not a new consultant. If the mitotic count was recorded on the lung core alone, note that a core underestimates mitotic activity relative to a resection.

feature: ER and PR <1% by IHC (decision-relevant negative)
test_name: Retrieval of the ER and PR IHC report: specimen of origin (2024 uterine resection versus 2026 lung core), antibody clone, scoring system and internal control adequacy, with a repeat stain on the metastasis if the call came from the primary
rationale: The ER and PR result is recorded as confirmed at under 1 percent, which forecloses the endocrine branch, but the profile does not say which specimen produced it. Hormone-receptor expression in uterine leiomyosarcoma can differ between a uterine primary and a distant metastasis, and a 2024 primary is the specimen where a positive would be more likely, not less. If the call came from the lung core, nothing more is needed; if it came from the 2024 uterus, a repeat on the metastasis is the cheap way to be sure the door is genuinely shut.
turnaround_estimate: days for the report; 3-5 days for a repeat stain
tissue_required_estimate: no new tissue for the records request; 2 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core if a repeat is warranted
decision_gated: Whether aromatase inhibition stays foreclosed; a records question first, an assay only if the answer points at the 2024 block.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Only relevant if a repeat stain is warranted; report retrieval comes first and costs nothing.

notes: Ask for the percentage and intensity rather than a binary call. A 0 percent and a 1 percent read differently in a borderline discussion even though both are negative at the stated cutoff.

feature: HLA-A*02:01 confirmed present - opens the A*02:01-restricted TCR-T axis, one step behind antigen-expression testing
test_name: Tumor HLA loss-of-heterozygosity assessment from the tissue sequencing data (allele-specific HLA copy number)
rationale: Germline typing says which alleles she inherited; it says nothing about whether the tumor still presents them. Somatic loss of the A*02:01 allele is a documented escape route for the whole HLA-restricted antigen class and would undercut every A*02:01-directed option at once, however strong the antigen stain. Most comprehensive tissue panels can report allele-specific HLA copy number if asked, so this is a request to the laboratory rather than a separate assay.
turnaround_estimate: no additional time if requested with tissue order A
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; no additional specimen beyond tissue order A
decision_gated: Whether A*02:01-restricted TCR-T and ImmTAC options remain viable if antigen expression is positive.

providers.notes: Exome-scale data supports allele-specific HLA copy-number inference; ask for it explicitly, since it is not on the standard report.

feature: Bilateral pulmonary metastases with an infiltrative, possibly inflammatory radiologic pattern
test_name: PD-L1 IHC with the clone and scoring system matched to the intended agent, plus CD3 and CD8 T-cell infiltrate density, on the 2026 pulmonary metastasis core
rationale: PD-L1 gates no approval in soft tissue sarcoma, so this informs rather than decides. It earns a row because the pulmonary lesions were read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory, and an immune phenotype on the lung core is the only way to tell whether that radiologic impression corresponds to anything in the tissue. Infiltrate density is also what cell-therapy and bispecific programs look at when weighing a candidate, so the CD3 and CD8 reads carry more forward here than the PD-L1 score does.
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 2-3 unstained slides from the 2026 lung core specifically
decision_gated: Supporting context for any checkpoint-blockade or cell-therapy proposal; MSI and TMB, not PD-L1, are what would open checkpoint blockade here.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Runs the PD-L1 companion clones and the CD3/CD8 stains on one requisition.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108-1221

notes: Use the lung core, not the 2024 uterus: the question is the current immune phenotype of the disease being treated. A PD-L1 result generated for one companion diagnostic does not transfer to another indication, so match the clone to whichever agent is actually under discussion. Tissue order B, the one IHC block cut: INI1/SMARCB1, MMR (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6), p53, Rb, ATRX, PD-L1 and B7-H3.
